_**Moana 2**_[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-5) is a 2024 American animated musical [adventure film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adventure_film "Adventure film") directed by [David Derrick Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Derrick_Jr. "David Derrick Jr."), Jason Hand, and Dana Ledoux Miller and written by Miller and [Jared Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jared_Bush "Jared Bush"). Produced by [Walt Disney Animation Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Animation_Studios "Walt Disney Animation Studios"), it is the second animated film in the [_Moana_ franchise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_\(franchise\) "Moana \(franchise\)"), following the [2016 film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_\(2016_film\) "Moana \(2016 film\)"). Most of the principal cast members reprise their roles including [Dwayne Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwayne_Johnson "Dwayne Johnson"), [Auliʻi Cravalho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auli%CA%BBi_Cravalho "Auliʻi Cravalho"), [Rachel House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_House "Rachel House"), [Temuera Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temuera_Morrison "Temuera Morrison"), [Nicole Scherzinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicole_Scherzinger "Nicole Scherzinger") and [Alan Tudyk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Tudyk "Alan Tudyk"). Set three years after the first film, it follows Moana reuniting with the demigod Maui and assembling a wayfinding crew to find the lost island of Motufetu, break its curse, and reconnect the people of the ocean.
A follow-up to 2016's _Moana_ was originally developed as a [miniseries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miniseries "Miniseries") for [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+"), but by February 2024, it had been reworked into a theatrical sequel. [Mark Mancina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Mancina "Mark Mancina") and [Opetaia Foaʻi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opetaia_Foa%CA%BBi "Opetaia Foaʻi"), the composers and co-songwriters of the first film, returned to score and co-write the songs, while [Abigail Barlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abigail_Barlow "Abigail Barlow") and [Emily Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Bear "Emily Bear") served as the main songwriters.
_Moana 2_ premiered at the Lanikuhonua Cultural Institute in [Kapolei, Hawaii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapolei,_Hawaii "Kapolei, Hawaii"), on November 21, 2024, and was released by [Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Studios_Motion_Pictures "Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures") in the United States on November 27. The film received mixed reviews from critics and grossed $1.059 billion worldwide, outgrossing its predecessor and becoming the [third highest-grossing film of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film#Highest-grossing_films "2024 in film"). It was nominated for [Best Animated Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Animated Feature Film") at the [82nd Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards "82nd Golden Globe Awards"). A sequel is in development.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-VarietyMoana3-6) [A live-action remake to the first film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_\(2026_film\) "Moana \(2026 film\)") was released in 2026.
## Plot
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&veaction=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section's source code: Plot")]
Three years after becoming a chieftess and [wayfinder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynesian_navigation "Polynesian navigation") for her people,[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-7) [Moana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_\(character\) "Moana \(character\)") spends her days exploring other islands near her home island of Motunui in the hope of finding people connected to the ocean. On her return from one such voyage, Moana is named Motunui's first _tautai_ (master wayfinder) in a thousand years.
In a vision, Moana's ancestor, Tautai Vasa, reveals why none of those people are connected anymore: the malicious storm god Nalo wanted power over the mortals, so he sunk a legendary island called Motufetu, which connected all of the islands, down to the depths of the ocean. Vasa further warns that the people of Motunui will go extinct in the future if Moana cannot find a way to raise Motufetu. In response to this call from the ancestors, Moana assembles a crew of people from Motunui — craftswoman Loto, historian Moni, and grumpy elderly farmer Kele, alongside her pet pig and rooster, Pua and Heihei — to follow the path of a comet across the ocean towards Motufetu.
Meanwhile, Maui is seeking Motufetu himself since he had a previous quarrel with Nalo, but he is captured by Nalo's enforcer, Matangi. Maui is reluctant to contact Moana, as he fears she may not survive if she comes to help. Moana and her crew are captured by the Kakamora, a tribe of savage coconut-like pirates that Moana previously encountered, who reveal that Nalo's actions against Motufetu had caused them to be disconnected from their home island. A Kakamora named Kotu helps the crew paralyze a gargantuan monster clam inside of which is Matangi's lair. While the crew finds Maui, Moana meets Matangi and learns that she is not happy serving Nalo. Matangi helps Moana escape and reunite with Maui and her friends, before sending them to where Nalo is.
Maui warns that Nalo's realm is deadlier compared to the mortal realm and that fighting him will spell certain death for mere mortals. Nalo's monsters ambush the group, damaging their raft and washing them ashore on an isolated island. Moana begins to despair, but Maui encourages her to keep on going. With Moana revitalized, the group plans to have Maui raise Motufetu so that Moana can touch it, as that is the only way to stop Nalo. Her crew repairs her raft, but when the group ventures forth to confront Nalo, they encounter a gigantic storm.
Moana, realizing that Nalo is trying to stop humans from breaking the curse, asks Maui to lift Motufetu enough for her to touch it. Maui begins to pull up Motufetu with his giant hook, but Nalo strips Maui of his demigod powers with a lightning bolt. Moana, in a moment of desperation, dives into the ocean to touch Motufetu underwater, but as she succeeds, Nalo's lightning kills her. Maui jumps in after her body, and with a magical chant, summons the spirits of Tautai Vasa and Moana's ancestors, including her grandmother Tala, who help revive her as a demigoddess, with Moana gaining a wayfinder's tattoo. Maui, also regaining his powers as a demigod, finally raises Motufetu and helps Moana reconnect the people with the ocean.
The crew returns home to Motunui, leading a flotilla of the people of the ocean, and a celebration is held in Moana's honor. Meanwhile, Nalo plans his revenge and is about to punish Matangi for helping Moana, when the giant crab Tamatoa arrives to join his cause.

In December 2020, during a Disney Investor Day meeting, [Walt Disney Animation Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Animation_Studios "Walt Disney Animation Studios") chief creative officer [Jennifer Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Lee_\(filmmaker\) "Jennifer Lee \(filmmaker\)") announced that a long-form musical comedy series titled _Moana: The Series_ , based on the [2016 film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_\(2016_film\) "Moana \(2016 film\)"), was in development at the studio and set for release on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+") in 2023.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-long-form-18)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Announcement-19) The series was to consist of five episodes.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Grimes-20) By August 2021, it was reported that [Osnat Shurer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osnat_Shurer "Osnat Shurer") would once again serve as producer.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-VancouverStudio-21) In January 2022, it was announced that [David Derrick Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Derrick_Jr. "David Derrick Jr."), storyboard artist for the first film, would serve as the writer and director.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-22)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-23)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-24) The series entered development simultaneously with [the live-action remake of _Moana_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_\(2026_film\) "Moana \(2026 film\)") according to [Jared Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jared_Bush "Jared Bush"), a writer of the film and screenplay writer of the 2016 animated film.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-25)
Dana Ledoux Miller came onto the series in early 2023 as a consulting writer, having finished writing the live-action remake with Bush, and turned in several revisions for the series.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-26)
According to Bush, the director and the writers repeatedly received feedback during development to the effect of: "We love this story. Why is it not going on the biggest screen you can possibly imagine?"[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Grimes-20) In January 2024, [Walt Disney Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Studios_\(division\) "Walt Disney Studios \(division\)") president Alan Bergman "informed the team that they needed to shift rapidly from making a five-episode streaming series to a second _Moana_ feature film".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Grimes-20) This last-minute "story pivot" was possible because nearly all the actual animation work for Disney animated films is not performed until the final year before the release date—everything before that is development.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Grimes-20)
In February 2024, [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney "Disney") CEO [Bob Iger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Iger "Bob Iger") officially announced that the series had been reworked into a theatrical sequel titled _Moana 2_ , with Derrick and Shurer remaining attached to the project.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Film-27) Iger explained that this occurred after Disney executives saw early footage: "We were impressed with what we saw and knew it deserved a theatrical release".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Rubin-28) By the release of the first trailer in May, Jason Hand and Dana Ledoux Miller were confirmed as co-directors alongside Derrick, while Christina Chen and [Yvett Merino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yvett_Merino "Yvett Merino") were revealed to replace Shurer as the film's producers.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-trailer-29)
### Casting
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&veaction=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Casting") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section's source code: Casting")]
Shortly after the announcement that the series was being repurposed into a theatrical feature film, [Auliʻi Cravalho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auli%CA%BBi_Cravalho "Auliʻi Cravalho") and [Dwayne Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwayne_Johnson "Dwayne Johnson") were confirmed to reprise their respective roles as [Moana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_\(character\) "Moana \(character\)") and [Maui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maui_\(Moana\) "Maui \(Moana\)").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Cravalho_CB-8)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Cravalho_SR-9)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Johnson_ET-11)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Johnson_X-12) Johnson later confirmed that he had been involved with the project since its conception, including its development, stating: "I can't wait for fans to see the film, the technology, the effects, cutting edge. We all really went for it. We thought if we're gonna make a sequel to something so beloved, let's really go for it."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Johnson_ET-11) Several more cast members were unveiled at the [Annecy International Animation Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annecy_International_Animation_Film_Festival "Annecy International Animation Film Festival"), including [Temuera Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temuera_Morrison "Temuera Morrison") and [Nicole Scherzinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicole_Scherzinger "Nicole Scherzinger") reprising their roles as Moana's parents from the first film. New additions include Khaleesi Lambert-Tsuda as Moana's new sister, and [Rose Matafeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Matafeo "Rose Matafeo"), [David Fane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Fane "David Fane"), and Hualālai Chung as members of Moana's wayfinding crew.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-lp614-13)
According to Cravalho, this film was the first time "that a [Disney princess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Princess "Disney Princess") has been allowed to age."[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-El-Mahmoud-30) When Cravalho returned to the [recording studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_studio "Recording studio") after the first film to record lines for Disney fireworks shows, Disney on Ice, and Lego Disney Princess, she was repeatedly asked to raise her vocal [pitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitch_\(music\) "Pitch \(music\)") to sound like herself as a teenager at age 16.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-El-Mahmoud-30) She was delighted when the film's directors allowed her to record Moana's lines at age 19 with her natural voice as a woman in her early twenties.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-El-Mahmoud-30)
### Animation
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&veaction=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Animation") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section's source code: Animation")]
Animation was handled at Walt Disney Animation Studios' Vancouver studio when it was being developed as a series, while pre-production and storyboarding took place at the Burbank studio.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-VancouverStudio-21) It is the first feature film to be made at the Vancouver studio.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-VancouverStudio-21)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-31) At the [Annecy International Animation Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annecy_International_Animation_Film_Festival "Annecy International Animation Film Festival"), it was revealed that veterans [Mark Henn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Henn "Mark Henn") and [Eric Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Goldberg_\(animator\) "Eric Goldberg \(animator\)") would supervise a team of apprentices of hand-drawn animators for Maui's tattoos. Goldberg was a supervising animator for "Mini Maui" for the first film.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-lp614-13)
In May 2025, [The Animation Guild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Animation_Guild "The Animation Guild") published a report estimating that as a result of Disney Animation's decision to largely outsource the animation work to its new Vancouver studio, California had lost as much as 817 jobs, $87 million in wages, and $178 million in state gross domestic product.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Kilkenny-32)
### Music
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&veaction=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Music") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section's source code: Music")]
Main article: [_Moana 2_ (soundtrack)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2_\(soundtrack\) "Moana 2 \(soundtrack\)")
[Mark Mancina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Mancina "Mark Mancina") and [Opetaia Foaʻi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opetaia_Foa%CA%BBi "Opetaia Foaʻi") returned to compose the [film score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_score "Film score"), while [Abigail Barlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abigail_Barlow "Abigail Barlow") and [Emily Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Bear "Emily Bear") contributed songs, replacing [Lin-Manuel Miranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin-Manuel_Miranda "Lin-Manuel Miranda") from the first film.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Lenker-33)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-34) Barlow and Bear are the youngest and the first all-female songwriting duo to write the songs for a Disney film.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Milzoff-35) Walt Disney Music president Tom MacDougall recruited Barlow and Bear in the fall of 2021, after hearing the quality of their work on _[The Unofficial Bridgerton Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Unofficial_Bridgerton_Musical "The Unofficial Bridgerton Musical")_ , and about a year later, in 2022, they began to work with the production team on writing songs.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Milzoff-35) Miranda assisted by providing Barlow with "a stack of books" on how to write lyrics for musical films.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Milzoff-35) Bear focused on studying the existing _Moana_ score, with its Polynesian [instrumentation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instrumentation_\(music\) "Instrumentation \(music\)"), and learning how to write songs with that musical vocabulary.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Milzoff-35) Cravalho stated that having Barlow and Bear, two young women, help voice Moana's "story, which is a young woman finding her way, I couldn't think of a better duo than Barlow and Bear. ... This is a new part of my voice. ... This film digs into these low notes in these times of indecision when we don't know what we are supposed to do next. There's a lot of deeper layers to these songs."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Lenker-33)
Miranda later explained that the reason he was not asked to return for the sequel came down to a matter of timing.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Pina-36) He was a longtime fan of _[The Lion King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lion_King "The Lion King")_ (1994) and desperately wanted to work on _[Mufasa: The Lion King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mufasa:_The_Lion_King "Mufasa: The Lion King")_ (2024), but director [Barry Jenkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Jenkins "Barry Jenkins") had to first wait six months for him.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Bahr-37) Miranda was simply too busy in the second half of 2021 with finishing the songs for _[Encanto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Encanto "Encanto")_ (2021), finishing up the editing of his [first feature film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tick,_Tick..._Boom!_\(film\) "Tick, Tick... Boom! \(film\)") as a director, and having to do press interviews to promote _Encanto_ and two other films.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Bahr-37) By the time Miranda was done with _Encanto_ interviews, he had to get started on _[Mufasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mufasa:_The_Lion_King "Mufasa: The Lion King")_ right away in early 2022.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Pina-36) Meanwhile, Disney Animation moved forward with Barlow and Bear, and they were "already cooking" by the time the decision was made to turn the streaming series into a feature-length sequel.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Pina-36)
On November 7, 2024, Disney revealed a full tracklist, along with the first single "Beyond" by Cravalho which was billed as a spiritual sequel to the original Moana anthem, "[How Far I'll Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Far_I'll_Go "How Far I'll Go")".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-beyondaulii-38) On November 11, Johnson revealed his song "Can I Get a Chee Hoo?" as a female empowerment song for Moana's character, which follows the tune of Maui's original "You're Welcome".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-cheehoorock-39) The Original Motion Picture Soundtrack was released on November 22.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-beyondaulii-38) "Beyond" and "Can I Get a Chee Hoo?" were nominated for the 2024 [Hollywood Music in Media Award for Best Original Song in an Animated Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Music_in_Media_Award_for_Best_Original_Song_in_an_Animated_Film "Hollywood Music in Media Award for Best Original Song in an Animated Film"),[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-40) and "Beyond" has been nominated for a 2025 [Society of Composers & Lyricists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_of_Composers_&_Lyricists "Society of Composers & Lyricists") Award for Outstanding Original Song for a Comedy or Musical Visual Media Production.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-41)

### Marketing
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&veaction=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Marketing") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section's source code: Marketing")]
The first trailer for the film was released on May 29, 2024, after debuting at [CinemaCon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Association_of_Theatre_Owners "National Association of Theatre Owners") the month before.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-trailer-29)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-44) The trailer earned over 178 million views in its first 24 hours across all platforms, breaking a new record as the most watched trailer of all time for a Disney animated film, a record previously held by _[Frozen 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frozen_2 "Frozen 2")_ and Pixar's _[Inside Out 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside_Out_2 "Inside Out 2")_ (the latter of which the trailer was attached to in the theaters).[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-45) A sneak peek of the film was screened at the [2024 Annecy International Animation Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Annecy_International_Animation_Film_Festival "2024 Annecy International Animation Film Festival") on June 14, 2024.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-46)
On August 9, 2024, Cravalho and Johnson appeared at the Disney Entertainment Showcase at the 2024 [D23 Expo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D23_\(Disney\) "D23 \(Disney\)") in [Anaheim, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaheim,_California "Anaheim, California") to promote the film and release a new trailer, which was released online shortly thereafter.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Giardina-47) During the D23 presentation, Cravalho performed a new song from the film, "We're Back," accompanied by Polynesian dancers.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Giardina-47) Johnson also used the presentation to announce a new live-action [Monster Jam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monster_Jam "Monster Jam") film that he would be producing with Disney.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-48)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&veaction=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Localization") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section's source code: Localization")]
Like the first film, _Moana 2_ was released in European countries[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-49)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-50)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-51) with the title and protagonist's name changed to _Vaiana_ due to a trademark conflict.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-52)
Four special [dubbings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubbing "Dubbing") in [Polynesian languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynesian_languages "Polynesian languages") were released for the sequel, in [Hawaiian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaiian_language "Hawaiian language"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-:0-10) [Māori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C4%81ori-language "Māori-language"),[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-53) [Tahitian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tahitian_language "Tahitian language"), and [Samoan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samoan_language "Samoan language").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-54) The first three languages had previously received a dubbing of the first film,[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-:2-55)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-56)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-:3-57) while a Samoan dubbing of the sequel was released without the original film having been dubbed. Cravalho reprised the lead role in the Hawaiian dubbing of the sequel,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-:0-10) like she did in the first film,[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-:3-57) while several other members of the cast reprised their roles in the Māori dubbing.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-58)
Of the six films dubbed into Māori so far,[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-59)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-60) _Moana 2_ is the first to have premiered in [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand") simultaneously in English and Māori.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-61) This marks the third time in Disney's history a dubbing in an indigenous language is released at the same time as regular dubbings. The first such instance happened with the Tahitian dubbing of _Moana_ , released in 2016 in [French Polynesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Polynesia "French Polynesia").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-:2-55) The second was the [Sámi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A1mi_languages "Sámi languages") dubbing of _[Frozen 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frozen_2 "Frozen 2")_ , released in 2019 in [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland "Finland"), [Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway "Norway"), and [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden "Sweden").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-62)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-63)
### Home media
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&veaction=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Home media") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section's source code: Home media")]
_Moana 2_ was released as a digital download on January 28, 2025, began streaming on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+") on March 12, 2025, and was released on [4K Ultra HD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra_HD_Blu-ray "Ultra HD Blu-ray"), [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray"), and [DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD "DVD") on March 18.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-64)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-65)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-66)
In the United Kingdom, _Moana 2_ debuted at No. 1 on the [Official Film Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_Charts_Company "Official Charts Company") based on digital downloads,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-67) remaining at the top for a second consecutive week with over 33,000 copies sold.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-68)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-69) In the United States, it topped both the [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes") and [Fandango at Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fandango_at_Home "Fandango at Home") charts for the week ending February 2.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-70) The film maintained the number-one position on both charts in its second week.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-71)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-72) For 2025, _Moana 2_ ranked seventh overall on Fandango at Home's digital sales and rentals chart.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-73) In physical media for 2025, _Moana 2_ ranked fifteenth on the Top Selling Titles on Disc (DVD + Blu-ray) of 2025, according to [Circana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circana "Circana") VideoScan. The film achieved a sales index of 32.61 compared to the year's top-selling title. Blu-ray formats made up 44% of total unit sales, while 4K Ultra HD accounted for 4%.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-74)
On Disney+, _Moana 2_ garnered 27.3 million views in its first five days, becoming the third-highest launch ever for a theatrical film on the platform and the best launch for a Walt Disney Animation Studios title since _[Encanto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Encanto "Encanto")_ in December 2021.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-75)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-76) [Nielsen Media Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_Media_Research "Nielsen Media Research"), which records streaming viewership on some U.S. television screens, reported that the film accumulated 1.9 billion minutes of watch time between March 10–16, making it the most-streamed film that week.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-77)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-78) _Moana 2_ was subsequently the sixth most-streamed title overall in March 2025, with 3.9 billion minutes viewed.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-79)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-80) Between January and June 2025, the film reached a total of 7.227 billion minutes streamed, ranking as the most-streamed film during that period.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-81)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-82) In December 2025, Disney announced that it was the most-watched film of the year on Disney+, with more than 80 million views.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-83)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-84) Nielsen later reported that _Moana 2_ was the second most-streamed film overall in 2025, with 9.43 billion minutes of watch time.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-85)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-86)
## Reception
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&veaction=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Reception") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section's source code: Reception")]
### Box office
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&veaction=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Box office") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section's source code: Box office")]
_Moana 2_ grossed $460.4 million in the United States and Canada, and $598.8 million in other territories, for a total of $1.059 billion worldwide.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-NUM-87)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-BOM-4) _[Deadline Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadline_Hollywood "Deadline Hollywood")_ calculated the film's net profit as $415 million, accounting for production budgets, marketing, talent participations and other costs; box office grosses, television and streaming, and home media revenues, making _Moana 2_ the second-most profitable film of 2024.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-88)
In the United States and Canada, _Moana 2_ was originally projected to gross $105–115 million over the five-day [Thanksgiving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanksgiving_\(United_States\) "Thanksgiving \(United States\)") weekend.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-89) After making $57.8 million on its first day (including $13.8 million from Tuesday night previews, both the highest-ever for a Walt Disney Animation film and Thanksgiving week release), five-day estimates were raised to $175–200 million.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-previewboxoffice-90) It then made a record $28 million on Thanksgiving, nearly doubling the 2019 film _[Frozen 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frozen_2 "Frozen 2")_ 's previous high of $14.9 million.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-HR-91) It went on to debut to $139.8 million (and a total of $225 million over the five days), breaking _Frozen 2_ 's $130.3 million record for the best opening weekend for a Walt Disney Animation film and a Thanksgiving weekend release, as well as nearly matching the entire domestic run of the first film ($248.7 million).[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-opening-92) The worldwide five-day gross of $389 million surpassed the 2023 film _[The Super Mario Bros. Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Super_Mario_Bros._Movie "The Super Mario Bros. Movie")_ as the highest such opening for an animated film.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-93) In its second weekend the film made $52 million (a drop of 62.8%), remaining in first.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-94)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-95) In its third weekend, the film retained the top spot again, grossing $26.6 million (dropping 48% from its second weekend).[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-96) The film was finally dethroned in its fourth weekend, grossing $13.1 million and finishing in fourth place.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-97)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-98) On January 19, 2025, the film crossed the $1 billion threshold, becoming the third film released in 2024 to do so.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-99)
### Critical response
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&veaction=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Critical response") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moana_2&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section's source code: Critical response")]
On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 61% of 245 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 6.0/10. The website's consensus reads: "Riding high on a wave of stunning animation even when its story runs adrift, _Moana 2_ isn't as inspired as the original but still delights as a colorful adventure."[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-100) [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean"), assigned the film a score of 58 out of 100, based on 50 critics, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Metacritic-101) Audiences polled by [CinemaScore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CinemaScore "CinemaScore") gave the film an average grade of "A–" on an A+ to F scale (down from the first's A), while those surveyed by [PostTrak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PostTrak "PostTrak") gave it an 89% overall positive score, with 64% saying they would "definitely recommend" it.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-opening-92)
Writing for _CinemaBlend_ , Dirk Libbey praised _Moana 2_ as "a really good movie", but also noted that it was too obvious that the film had been originally written as a much longer television series and then trimmed down for release as a feature film.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Libbey-102) Libbey pointed out that the film introduces viewers to several interesting characters like Matangi, Loto, Kele, and Moni, but fails to explore their backstories: the kind of subplots that would be "exactly where I would start" to cut if asked to condense several television scripts into a film script.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-Libbey-102)
Radheyan Simonpillai ([Globe and Mail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Globe_and_Mail "The Globe and Mail")) found the music flat and uninspired. Alison Willmore (Vulture) argued the film suffers from a lack of tension, part of Disney's recent trend away from colorful villains in favor of softer, internal conflicts. Owen Gleiberman ([Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety \(magazine\)")) called it "an okay movie" and "efficient enough" to be a holiday hit, though far more product-like than its predecessor.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2#cite_note-103)
